clauses.reason: Terminated by express revocation. EO 12553, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, official Federal Register text held), orders that the listed Executive Orders, "and any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and its number column lists 9702 (the held American Presidency Project transcription pairs 9702 with the subject 'Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute'). The wording has no effective-date clause, so the recorded date is the signing date 1986-02-25 (printed March 3, 1986, the alternative reading). Disclosed note: the order was functionally spent earlier, when the board reported and the standstill ran out; the report date is not held.

research_rationale:
Identity and text: read in full in the registered Federal Register original (11 FR, issue of 1946-03-12; grade original_representation_unverified, acceptable_as_original true). Order 9702 of March 8, 1946 creates an emergency board of three members under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute between the Alton Railroad Company and other carriers and employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, directs a report within thirty days of the order, and recites the statutory no-change period of thirty days after the report. Inventory: one sole paragraph. End: EO 12553, signed February 25, 1986, orders, in the official Federal Register text (51 FR 7237, held), that the listed Executive Orders, "and any amendments thereto, are revoked:", and its number column lists 9702; the held American Presidency Project transcription (corroboration only, not cited as evidence) pairs 9702 with the subject 'Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute'. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (report deadlines) the report date and the end of the standstill are spent facts, not ends; the order ends on the express revocation. No held source records when the board reported; if it reported by its deadline of April 7, 1946, the standstill ended by May 7, 1946. Functionally spent no later than 1946-05-07 on that assumption, which is not established by a held source.
